boundary.reason: RapidJSON's GenericDocument parser and traversal API are C++; one extern C call translates the completed observation into a fixed-width record.
boundary.abi_test: test.sh checks C and Ada layout, symbols, nullability, ownership, arbitrary Ada bounds, strictness, and failure publication.

portable.reason: C++17 with -O3 and no host-specific ISA compile flag.

native.reason: The portable flags add -mcpu=native on arm64/aarch64 and -march=native elsewhere.

limitations: The admitted call constructs and recursively traverses a DOM.
The adapter deliberately uses the ordinary owned DOM API rather than presenting DOM traversal as a streaming event API.
RapidJSON receives one complete contiguous input without adapter concatenation.

lanes.api: flyology_json_bench_rapidjson_dom uses GenericDocument::Parse with kParseValidateEncodingFlag and recursively visits every DOM value.
lanes.observable_result: Checksum over decoded strings, names, value kinds, and container counts plus event, scalar, member-name, and exact input-byte counters.
limitations: DOM allocation, string copying, number conversion, recursive traversal, and per-call cleanup are timed.
The adapter does not expose number lexemes or error offsets.
An initial UTF-8 BOM is accepted and ignored, so BOM fixtures are profile-disagreement evidence rather than primary throughput inputs.
No RapidJSON writer boundary is included.
No RapidJSON writer boundary is included.
No combined parse-and-write boundary is included.

other_limits: Input and DOM size are bounded by size_t, address space, and available allocation.
No explicit depth ceiling is configured; RapidJSON and the adapter consume allocator and native-stack resources.
